## Career
### 2010s: _Full Dark, No Stars_ to _The Institute_
[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-68) Later that year, he published _[Doctor Sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_Sleep_(novel))_, a sequel to _The Shining._

During his Chancellor's Speaker Series talk at [University of Massachusetts Lowell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Massachusetts_Lowell) on December 7, 2012, King said that he was writing a crime novel about a retired policeman being taunted by a murderer, with the working title _[Mr. Mercedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Mercedes)_. [[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-71) He returned to horror with _[Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revival_(novel))_, which he called "a nasty, dark piece of work". [[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-74) In 2018, he released _[The Outsider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Outsider_(King_novel))_, which features the character [Holly Gibney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_Gibney), and the novella _[Elevation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevation_(novella))_.

### 2020s: _If It Bleeds_ to present
[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-76) In 2022, King released the novel _[Fairy Tale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fairy_Tale_(novel))_. _[Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holly_(novel))_, about Holly Gibney was released in September 2023. [[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-Combined_Print_&_E-Book_Fiction-79) King released _[Never Flinch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Flinch)_, featuring Holly Gibney, in 2025.

## Collaborations
### Literature
[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_King#cite_note-97) King and his son [Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_King) co-wrote _[Sleeping Beauties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeping_Beauties_(novel))_ (2018), set in a West Virginia women's prison.
